note: Inputs of the excited-states article's plates (src/content/work/figures/excited-states/), one entry per file. source_path is under archive_root, read-only; md5 and size_bytes are of the committed file, source_md5 of the file it was copied from. Private documents are not among them.

3BSD.pdb.what: PDB 3BSD, 'Light harvesting protein from RC of Chlorobium tepidum' (HEADER 23-DEC-07, released 22-JAN-08, 2.30 A): the FMO complex, one protein chain A (2,798 ATOM records) with eight bacteriochlorophyll a residues (BCL A 367-373 of 66 atoms each, A 400 of 42 atoms; 504 atoms), one magnesium ion (MG A 374, HETATM 3262, occupancy 0.33, its CONECT partners three waters) and 178 HOH. Ben-Shem, Frolow, Nelson, FEBS Lett. 564, 274 (2004), doi:10.1016/S0014-5793(04)00360-6. The file is the PDB's own, as downloaded in October 2015; its AUTHOR record spells Ben-Shem 'BRN-SHEM'.
3BSD.pdb.edit: none; a verbatim copy. Until 2026-10-15 the lone magnesium ion HETATM 3262 was deleted by hand so it would not draw as a loose sphere; the deposited file is now kept as it is and render_box_grid.prepare leaves the ion out by rule: a one-atom HETATM residue of a metal (constants.METALS) bonded to no other hetero atom is not drawn. The subject PDB prepare writes for the hero is byte-identical either way, so the render is unaffected.
3BSD.pdb.checked_before_use: chain A only (2,798 ATOM records), 8 BCL residues with 504 atoms, 178 HOH, no HETATM outside BCL and HOH but the one MG ion, 522 CONECT records in the source (none are read), no alternate locations

chromophore-1.xyz.what: FMO bacteriochlorophyll a no. 1 as the JCTC 2017 calculations used it: 76 atoms (33 C, 34 H, 1 Mg, 4 N, 4 O), phytyl tail replaced by methyl, the LC-wPBE/6-31G** geometry superposed on the crystal frame (Fornari, Rowe, Padula, Troisi, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 13, 3754 (2017), p.4-5; thesis p.16). Mg at 46.20, 152.12, 136.71. Its coordinates match neither local PDB frame (3BSD, 3ENI), consistent with the P. aestuarii entry 3EOJ, which is not on disk: the plate that uses it must not name the organism or the entry.
chromophore-1.xyz.edit: none; a verbatim copy, name lower-cased with a hyphen
chromophore-1.xyz.format_quirk: Count line '76', blank comment line, space-separated columns.

chromophore-2.xyz.what: FMO bacteriochlorophyll a no. 2, as chromophore-1.xyz. The all-atom minimum separation from chromophore 1 is 2.2613 A (an oxygen and a hydrogen), the 2.26 A of the paper's Table 1, pair 1-2.
chromophore-2.xyz.edit: none; a verbatim copy, name lower-cased with a hyphen
chromophore-2.xyz.format_quirk: Count line '76', blank comment line, space-separated columns.

fmo-natural.xyz.what: The natural arrangement of the eight FMO bacteriochlorophyll a, 608 atoms (264 C, 272 H, 8 Mg, 32 N, 32 O; eight chromophores of 76 atoms), centred on the mean of its 608 atoms (the origin to 0.01 angstrom; the midpoint of the source and drain magnesium is 4.9 angstrom from it, so it is not centred there, as an earlier version of this entry said); identical to Geometries/Geometry_00001.xyz, structure 1 of the library of Knee, Rowe, Smith, Troisi, Datta, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 8, 2328 (2017).
fmo-natural.xyz.format_quirk: The count line is the atom count plus a tab, the comment line is blank, columns are tab-separated and the element symbol is padded with a space. boxprep.read_xyz reads the file as it is (it splits on any whitespace and skips the comment line), so no extension was needed; scripts/tests/test_excited_states_data_provenance.py reads the staged files through it.

fmo-generated-00300.xyz.what: Structure 300 of the 50,000 generated rearrangements of the eight chromophores (Geometries/Geometry_00001.xyz to Geometry_50000.xyz, dated 2017-01-19), same composition as the natural arrangement; source and drain (BChl 1 and 3) are at the same positions as in every file checked, the other six move. The JPCL paper's Fig. 1 shows structures 100, 200 and 300.
fmo-generated-00300.xyz.format_quirk: The count line is the atom count plus a tab, the comment line is blank, columns are tab-separated and the element symbol is padded with a space. boxprep.read_xyz reads the file as it is (it splits on any whitespace and skips the comment line), so no extension was needed; scripts/tests/test_excited_states_data_provenance.py reads the staged files through it.

table1-short-range-share.json.source_path: ../papers/excitonic-interactions/paper.pdf (the WRAP accepted manuscript of the JCTC paper, outside the archive; PDF page = manuscript page + 1)
table1-short-range-share.json.source_pointer: JCTC paper (Fornari, Rowe, Padula and Troisi, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 13, 3754 (2017)), Table 1, manuscript p.11 (PDF p.12); the 7 A threshold is on manuscript p.9.
table1-short-range-share.json.what: The fifteen own-data rows of Table 1 of Fornari, Rowe, Padula and Troisi, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 13, 3754 (2017): system (FMO, LH2, PCP), pair, minimum distance D in angstrom, coupled states, J_TOT and J_short in meV and the printed share J_short/J_TOT. FMO's D equal the all-atom minima of the archive's chromophore files (pair 1-2: 2.261 A).
table1-short-range-share.json.edit: Typed from the page into JSON; not a copy of a file. The two Scholes et al. comparison rows of LH2 are left out.

renders.note: Why each committed render looks as it does; free-form, read by people. The values in manifest.json are the record, test_excited_states_data_provenance.py checks that these agree with them.
renders.method: World +z is the image's up and render_box_grid.py does not rotate a structure, so candidate directions were generated rather than guessed: about 6,000 random points on the sphere (those within 18 degrees of the z axis dropped), orthographic projection of all 3,302 atoms at 1728 x 972 with margin 1.02, scored by scale (px per angstrom) and by the share of the 40 macrocycle atoms (the eight Mg and their 32 pyrrole N) that no backbone atom (N, CA, C, O; a 2 angstrom disc) lies in front of by more than 1 angstrom. The scoring script was a scratch one and is not committed; the numbers below are its output. Four well-separated directions were draft-rendered (--draft, 864 x 486; the four in one run took 17 min 55 s, 255 to 282 s each on 32 CPU cores) and the choice was made by eye on those drafts, then rendered at the production tier. 2026-10-09.

hero.why: Chain A is a shell of beta-sheet and helices around the eight bacteriochlorophylls, and this view looks level across the open face of the shell: the central stack of seven pigments shows through between the helices and the eighth (A 400, 42 atoms, its tail unmodelled) sits at the left edge with a helix across its lower half. It is the 2026-10-09 choice, [-0.7, 0.71, 0.14], brought level by the design review: molrender fits its orthographic camera to the projected corners of the subject's bounding box, not to the atoms, so a view with any z component also frames the box's top face, and on this subunit, whose height (59.8 angstrom along z) fixes the 16:9 frame's scale, the 0.14 cost a sixth of the scale. Level, the scale is the frame's height over the subunit's. The margin is 1.06, not the plate default 1.02: level at 1.02 the ink reached 9 px from the top and bottom edges (0.98 of the height) and read as cropped on the page; at 1.06 it covers 0.94. The sticks are the palette's carbon (render_box_grid.py's rule since this review; they were magnesium's dark green, the darkest colour present, so each magnesium sphere merged with its bonds). Nothing is clipped: the frame is fitted to the subunit.

candidates.verdict: The eighth pigment shows on the left but the central stack is partly behind the sheet's front strands, and the lower-left pigments are hidden by two helices. Rejected.
Looks up into the shell from below: the strands stack over the pigments and the composition reads as a bowl of beta-sheet with a few pigments inside it. Rejected.

Replaced by the design review (2026-10-09) with the same azimuth brought level, below. The eighth pigment stood clearer here, but the bounding-box fit framed the subunit at 13.25 px per angstrom (0.43 x 0.86 of the frame, 16 per cent of its area in ink); the 15.33 above is the atoms-only scoring, which the render does not follow.
Side-on to the sheet: the strands stack like the rungs of a ladder in front of the pigments, and one pigment is clear. Rejected.

Chosen. The design review's level view, margin 1.06: 15.32 px per angstrom by the bounding-box model (15.92 at margin 1.02, production 183 s, rejected for the 9 px edges), ink 0.50 x 0.94 of the frame and 20 per cent of its area. The stack reads through the open face; the eighth pigment keeps its upper half clear of a helix.

Level at azimuth 110 degrees, margin 1.02, picked because the backbone z-buffer found the eighth pigment wholly unoccluded there. Rejected: rendered, a helix crosses the eighth pigment, which is edge-on, and three helices lie across the stack, which reads darker and more crowded than at azimuth 135.

hero.limits: The macrocycle score is a crude backbone-only z-buffer (and it called the azimuth-110 eighth pigment clear when the cartoon covers it); the choice rests on the renders. In every direction tried between a fifth and a third of the macrocycle atoms are behind a helix or strand, and the stack at the centre is dense: the eight are not each separately countable in the frame, which is why the caption says the pigments sit inside the protein rather than number them off the picture, and at the common sphere radius few magnesium showed, the rings being seen obliquely; since 2026-10-17 magnesium is drawn at 4 times the radius and all 8 show. The subunit is nearly square in projection and the frame 16:9, so the ink covers half the width at most; the hero is never cropped (spec 6.2). The scale figures are the bounding-box model's (the corners of the atoms' axis-aligned box projected along the direction, which reproduces each render's ink box to 0.01 of the frame); the scoring script was a scratch one and is not committed. The one non-white border pixel, at the top right, is Molecular Nodes' known compositor stray (render_box_grid.py's docstring) and passes the border check.

radii.why: The plate's values (the carbon plates'), not overridden. A production render at 0.6 and 0.3 was made for comparison (220 s) and the pigments clumped into a mass of spheres in which the rings could no longer be followed; 0.4 and 0.22 keep each ring's outline. Since 2026-10-17 magnesium alone is drawn at 4 times sphere_radius_angstrom (manifest sphere_scale, Patrick's instruction), so the one at the centre of each pigment shows.

ligand_bonds.why: Molecular Nodes bonds a residue from biotite's templates, which know the twenty amino acids and nothing of BCL in this older file, and 3BSD carries no CONECT for them: the first draft drew the eight BCL as 504 unbonded spheres. render_box_grid.prepare now writes a CONECT record for every bond boxprep.find_bonds finds among the hetero atoms (568: 74 in each of seven residues and 50 in the eighth), and the render draws them as sticks.

hero.rig: Rendered 2026-10-17 on Patrick's instruction ("Make them bright purple. Make them 4x larger. Improve the rendering quality - ensure principled bsdf, lighting from the side/underneath to add depth. MInimum 5x bouces. cycles rendering. ambient occlusion on."): Cycles, molrender's PRODUCTION tier with diffuse and glossy bounces 5 and Fast GI kept on but taking over only at bounce 5 (ao_bounces_render 5, fast_gi_method REPLACE; Blender's default of bounce 1 had left the earlier renders one real bounce); the three-point key at 2 W, the studio HDRI at 0.8, a sun fill of 1.5 W/m², a side light of 12 W and a light from below at 8 W (molrender Light.under_power); every material molrender's Principled BSDF Solid at the matte settings (roughness 0.9, specular 0.15, no coat, no subsurface); magnesium #a64bf4 at 4 times the sphere radius (sphere_scale), cartoon chain A #3f6e5b. molrender at commit 4b26311 (branch fix-masked-layer-collision; '-dirty' in the summary line is an unrelated uncommitted edit to molrender's render guide), Molecular Nodes 4.5.13. An ADD Fast GI variant was rendered and rejected: its darkest tenth of ink pixels was about 40% lighter (luma p10 68 against 49), flattening the crevices. The 2026-10-15 render it replaces drew magnesium dark green #1f3f21 at the common radius, and a moss-green #7d9150 trial earlier on 2026-10-17 showed about 3 of the 8 where unoccluded.
